title: Cryptography: digests, symmetric and asymmetric ciphers and `KeyStore`

videos.script: Cryptography in the JDK is a set of tools, and the hard part is choosing the right one, with the right settings. This lesson uses four, and never invents any. {{digest}} A digest is a fingerprint. The same bytes always give the same thirty-two, and one changed letter changes half of them. {{seal}} A cipher keeps a secret. AES in GCM mode encrypts, and also notices when somebody changed a single bit of what it encrypted. {{sign}} A signature proves who wrote something. The library signs with a private key, and anybody holding the public key can check, but nobody can forge. {{store}} And keys have to live somewhere. A keystore is a file that holds them, locked with a password that comes from the environment, never from the code. One rule runs through all of it: use what the JDK provides, the way it is meant to be used.
